newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Telesis proposes rate reduction.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Telesis proposes rate reduction.

text.p: Pacific Telesis Group's Pacific Bell Monday said it filed a proposal with the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to lower its local toll prices for business and residential customers, as well as its switched access prices for long-distance customers by about $305 million.

In a statement, the company said the proposed price reductions result from the CPUC's recent creation of a $352 million fund to support Universal Service statewide. Because Pacific Bell will receive some $305 million from the Fund, the company said it has proposed reducing its rates accordingly.

Universal service is a series of subsidies by which basic emergency and incoming calls are provided at low cost to those on welfare. Regulatory rules also apply a general series of cross subsidies from urban to rural users, from business to residential, from optional services to basic services and from long-distance to local calling.
The company's plan must now be approved by the Commission before it becomes effective.
Under the proposed new rates, a direct dial five minute call from a residence between San Francisco and San Jose will would cost $0.46, down from $0.59 at current rates.
